newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swissair to decide Sabena write-off April.
newsitem.headline: Swissair to decide Sabena write-off April.

text.p: SAirGroup, the holding company for the Swissair airline, said Sabena's annual 1996 result was poor and it would decide whether to write off its investment in the Belgian carrier sometime in April.
Howerver, SAirGroup also said in a comment on Sabena's results that it expects 1997 results to "improve substantially" and that Sabena's break-even point will be reached in 1998.

Earlier today Sabena, 49.5 percent owned by Swissair, reported a 1996 loss after provisions of 8.87 billion Belgian francs ($251.5 million), up from 1995's loss of 1.66 billion, and said it still aimed to return to profitability in 1998.
"The SAirGroup expects, however, that the financial results for its Belgian partner will improve substantially in the current year and that the break-even point will be met in 1998," SAirGroup said.
Progress will be possible through a variety of measures with emphasis on cost-cutting efforts and enhancing flight traffic through an optimised route network.

"It is in the best interest of Swissair and the other companies of the SAirGroup to increase the already close coopration with Sabena while taking advantage of the resulting synergies," SAirGroup said.
SAirGroup and Sabena have already achieved cooperation in cargo, catering technology and sales and station organisation, and both partners are also benefiting from cooperation with Delta Air Lines.
"The SAirGroup plans to continue working closely with Sabena at various levels, irrespective of any pending decision concerning a write-off of its investment in the Belgian airline," SAirGroup said.
Swissair bought the stake in Sabena for around 270 million francs and consolidates Sabena at equity in its results.
Losses at Sabena therefore directly hit SAGroup's results, already under pressure from losses in the flight operations of the Swissair airline.

Industry analysts expect Swissair to write off much of its investment in Sabena, but this is largely seen as an accounting measure to reduce the negative impact of Sabena's losses in 1997 on SAirGroup.
SAirGroup will release key financial results on April 4, following a board meeting earlier in the week.
